name: workspace-root-project-registry
purpose: Registry of root-level projects, their ownership boundaries, project-local homes, shared dependencies, and operating notes.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry to decide whether work belongs in an existing root project, a reserved underscore operations folder, or a new root project.
how_to_read: Find the project by name or path.
Read purpose and scope before placing files.
Use project_specific_home to decide where project-local code, docs, configs, assets, tests, and artifacts belong.
Use shared_dependencies and boundary_notes to avoid mixing project-specific and shared workspace assets.
update_triggers: A root project is created, archived, renamed, or removed.
A project starts depending on a shared tool, template, skill, or asset library.
Structure audit or workspace map output shows an unregistered root project.

reference_links.title: Project Boundary Management Workflow
used_for: preventing project-specific files from drifting into shared folders

structure_rules.rule: Each projects entry must describe one root-level non-reserved project folder.
structure_rules.reason: Root project registration keeps workspace ownership clear as projects multiply.

structure_rules.rule: Each active project should list project_specific_home paths for its code, docs, configs, assets, tests, and artifacts.
structure_rules.reason: Future agents need to know where to put files without relying on chat history.

structure_rules.rule: Boundary notes should explain what belongs in the project and what must stay in shared operations folders.
structure_rules.reason: This prevents domain-specific assets and shared platform assets from being mixed accidentally.

field_guide.meaning: Registered root projects and their boundaries.
Project-owned folders where project-specific code, docs, configs, assets, tests, and artifacts should live.
Shared workspace folders or projects this project may reference without owning.
Operational notes for avoiding ownership drift.

projects.name: agent-platform
projects.purpose: Central Python-first platform project for building, configuring, evaluating, and improving agents.
projects.scope: Reusable platform models, agent specs, evaluation helpers, planning helpers, open-source evaluation, and platform docs.
boundary_notes: Platform-wide reusable capabilities can live here when they are part of the central agent platform.
Domain-specific experiments should become separate root projects instead of being added to agent-platform by default.

projects.name: presentation-agent
projects.purpose: Presentation-focused agent project for collecting presentation design references, PPT/HTML sources, reusable assets, and script-flow evidence.
projects.scope: Presentation reference catalogs, project-specific presentation research, PPTX-to-HTML conversion helpers, presentation asset storage policy, and future presentation script/flow agents.
boundary_notes: Keep presentation-specific data, conversions, and generated artifacts inside presentation-agent/.
Store raw PPT/PPTX/assets only after project-local license review.
Reusable presentation reference curation behavior is tracked as a skill under _skills/.

projects.name: design-asset-library
projects.purpose: Reusable, legally cautious SVG design asset library for presentation decks, HTML artifacts, dashboards, prototypes, and platform visual systems.
projects.scope: Internally generated SVG packs, asset registry, source provenance, license guidance, usage guidance, generator scripts, and asset validation tests.
boundary_notes: Use generated SVG assets as the default legal-safe asset source.
Actually collected external SVG files belong under design-asset-library/assets/svg/external/ with source-level LICENSE and SOURCE.json files.
Do not store third-party SVG files unless license, source URL, access date, attribution, public-use constraints, upstream path, and pinned commit are recorded.
External source candidates are research leads until license review is complete.
Project-specific finished deck or UI artifacts stay in the owning project; reusable source SVG assets stay here.

projects.name: platform-desktop-app
projects.purpose: Desktop/installable software productization project for turning the workspace platform into an end-user application with OS-specific installer, release, privacy, and update gates.
projects.scope: Desktop product boundary, distribution registry, packaging strategy, installer release gates, project-local requirements/specs, and future desktop shell implementation.
boundary_notes: End-user installer packaging belongs here, not in agent-platform install_mode setup profiles.
Use the selected Tauri-first scaffold around workspace-monitor unless measured release or maintenance evidence changes the decision.
Reuse workspace-monitor as the initial UI candidate unless desktop-specific research proves a separate UI is easier to maintain.
Do not bundle real secrets, private snapshots, or environment-specific tokens in installers.
Actual Tauri, Electron, or packager dependency installation must follow the installation audit workflow.

projects.name: workspace-monitor
projects.purpose: Vercel-deployable Next.js monitoring site that visualizes repository history, projects, agents, requirements, specs, evaluations, and Markdown documents from a generated workspace snapshot.
projects.scope: Project-local Next.js UI, repository snapshot generator, generated monitor data, deployment docs, tests, and monitor-specific requirements/specs.
boundary_notes: Keep monitor UI code, data collection scripts, generated snapshots, and deployment settings inside workspace-monitor/.
Read shared repository documents as data sources; do not move source histories or project docs into the monitor project.
Before deploying publicly, review generated snapshots for private data and regenerate only the documents intended for public visibility.
